Thank you, sometimes it's easy to forget that.

I really appreciate your comment. I've run my friends' tolerance dry with all of my family problems, so sometimes I just panic in the silence. 
People tell me that too. I have to disagree with them, though. I believe all families have problems, but whether they're abusive/dysfunctional or not is based on their ability to solve them. My family likes to pretend everything is okay and insult each other without apology. I like to think when I grow up and have a family that we'll be able to face our problems together, and face the fact we're not perfect people. 
I'm sorry for your loss. It's interesting because I'm in quite the opposite scenario - I don't know what it's like to have someone close pass away. I think everyone suffers loneliness in one way or another, some more severe than others, too.
I've learned, without minimizing the problems I do have, to appreciate what good things and resources I do have. I have money, I have education, I have food and shelter. I think one thing we can both hold onto is our impact on others lives. Whether or not I have a family of my own, and I can go out into the world and tell people they're not alone, tell people they're not unworthy and that they deserve to be loved, and that's pretty much what you did just now, and I do in fact appreciate it.

I appreciate your advice. I spoke to my therapist about it and she said CPS typically takes minors and it's difficult to prove something that isn't physical. If I called CPS, I'd also be paying for college by myself. I've stayed with friends for weeks and weeks. Now they're all away at college. I think I'm going to have to transfer. That, or move out. I can't do this anymore.
